title: Read declarations, types, and failures
concepts: Separate declarations from calls: a class name is followed by a class body, while a constructor has parameters and no return type. Java supplies a no-argument constructor only when you declare no constructors.

Check an API's parameter count, types, and meanings. Font(String name, int style, int size) accepts two integers, so swapping style and size can compile without producing the intended font. Compilation is not proof of correctness.

Initialize local variables before reading them. A blank final instance field must be assigned exactly once on each normally completing constructor path. Allocating an object array creates slots initially containing null, not the objects for those slots.

Text must be parsed before numeric arithmetic. Malformed integer text causes NumberFormatException at runtime; integer division by zero causes ArithmeticException. Catch expected failures specifically. A finally block normally runs after either success or a handled failure.

An abstract method declares a contract with a semicolon, not a body. An interface can also contain default or static methods with bodies, and private helper methods since Java 9; not every implemented interface method is invalid.

title: Trace decisions, repetition, and arithmetic
concepts: An if/else-if chain selects its first true branch, so test narrow ranges before broader ones. Braces make branch ownership explicit. In a traditional colon-style switch, execution falls through unless a break or another exit stops it; fall-through is sometimes intentional.

Trace a for loop as initialization, condition, body, then update. A while loop tests before its body and may execute zero times; a do/while loop tests after its body. Make sure repeated work can eventually change the stopping condition.

Each outer-loop iteration starts a fresh inner-loop traversal. A print inside the inner loop contributes to one row; a println after that loop finishes the row. Bounds determine both the row and column counts.

Arithmetic follows grouping and operand types, not the result variable's type. Multiplication and division have equal precedence and associate left to right. Parenthesize a whole denominator, and convert an operand to double before dividing when you need a fraction.

A sentinel marks the end of input rather than another measurement. Exclude it from both sum and count, and guard an empty count before calculating an average. break exits the nearest loop; continue skips the rest of its current iteration.

title: Distinguish text values from mutable buffers
concepts: A String's contents cannot change. Operations such as concat, trim, and replace return a result; assigning that result changes which String a variable refers to, not the original String's contents.

Use equals to compare String contents. The == operator compares object references, so equal text in two separate objects need not pass an identity check. Interned literals can make incorrect identity comparisons appear to work.

StringBuffer edits a mutable object, so two references to the same buffer observe an append. Its methods are synchronized; that does not automatically make a sequence of several calls atomic. StringBuilder is the usual unsynchronized alternative for single-threaded text assembly.
The + operator is evaluated left to right. 1 + 2 + " stops" produces "3 stops", but "Stops: " + 1 + 2 produces "Stops: 12". Parenthesize arithmetic when joining it to text.

Input methods consume different amounts of text. Scanner.nextInt reads a numeric token and can leave the line ending behind; a following nextLine may read only that remainder. Reading whole lines and parsing them makes that boundary explicit.

title: Model state and specialize behavior
concepts: A class defines state and behavior; new creates an instance and invokes a constructor. Overloaded constructors have different parameter lists. this refers to the current instance, while super(...) selects a superclass constructor to initialize the superclass part.

Keep implementation details private and expose meaningful operations. An unrelated top-level class does not gain private access just by sharing a source file. A subclass can use accessible inherited methods without directly touching the parent's private fields.

Inheritance models an is-a relationship; a class has one direct superclass and may implement multiple interfaces. An abstract class may combine state, constructors, concrete methods, and abstract contracts. A concrete descendant must implement the remaining abstract methods.

The declared reference type determines which methods a call can name; the actual object's class selects an overridden instance implementation at runtime. @Override catches signature mistakes. Changing parameters overloads a method rather than overriding it, and an override cannot narrow access.

An instance field belongs to one object; a static field belongs to the class. final prevents reassignment of a variable, overriding of a method, or subclassing of a class, depending on its position. A final reference does not make the referenced object immutable.

Connect inheritance to Withdraw guard: a custom class extending Exception directly defines a checked exception type. throw raises an instance; throws declares the possibility, and callers must catch it or propagate it. It is not an interface implementation.

title: Build a window from components and containers
concepts: Choose components by responsibility: JLabel presents text, JTextField accepts text, and JButton offers an action. Creating a component does not display it; attach it to a container that is ultimately inside a visible window.

A layout manager sizes and positions children. FlowLayout arranges a row that can wrap, GridLayout gives equal-sized cells, and BorderLayout assigns regions. Nest panels for richer layouts rather than adding several independent children to the same BorderLayout region.

Use JComboBox for a compact item selection. ButtonGroup enforces mutual exclusion among radio buttons but is not a visible container; add those buttons to both the group and a panel. Independent check boxes represent choices that can coexist.

Menus form a tree: a JFrame installs a JMenuBar with setJMenuBar; the bar holds JMenus, and a JMenu holds items or another JMenu as a submenu. Nest the submenu inside its intended parent rather than alongside that parent on the bar.

Schedule Swing construction and updates on the event-dispatch thread with SwingUtilities.invokeLater. Configure the close operation, populate the window, then pack it and make it visible. pack uses preferred component sizes; it does not promise fixed pixel dimensions.

title: Turn a user action into a validated update
concepts: An event source notifies registered listeners using an event object. A JButton's action can come from keyboard activation as well as a mouse click, so ActionListener models the intended action more directly than a mouse-only listener.

Registration connects source to callback; merely defining actionPerformed does not subscribe a listener. ActionListener has one abstract method, so an anonymous class or a compatible lambda can provide the callback. A lambda body runs when notified, not when registered.

Separate reading, validation, calculation, and display. getText returns a String; parse it explicitly and report malformed input. A successfully parsed value can still be unsuitable, such as a nonpositive duration; floating-point inputs may also need finite-value checks.

Swing callbacks normally execute on the event-dispatch thread. Keep handlers short and update components there; long-running work belongs off that thread, with results returned safely, for example through SwingWorker.

State that survives clicks belongs in a lasting object, such as a counter field. A local variable captured by a lambda must be final or effectively final, but a captured component reference may still refer to an object whose text can be updated.
